title: The Demo Window and the Debug Tools
summary: Dear ImGui ships its best documentation as a program - `ShowDemoWindow` shows every widget with the code beside it. It also ships tools for finding your own bugs - the Metrics window, the ID Stack tool, the Item Picker and debug logs. This lesson shows how to use them all.
markdown:
## ShowDemoWindow

```cpp-norun
ImGui::ShowDemoWindow();
```

One call opens a window that demonstrates almost every feature of ImGui: widgets, layout, tables, popups, drag and drop, styling, fonts. It is the **real documentation**: when you want to know how to do something, find it in the demo window, then open `imgui_demo.cpp` and search for the label you saw. The code you need is right there.

The demo's **"Tools"** menu (top of the window) opens the other tools below.

Keep `imgui_demo.cpp` in every project during development; it costs nothing until called. Leave the call out of shipping builds (lesson 6.03).

## The style editor

```cpp-norun
ImGui::ShowStyleEditor();
```

Every size, rounding and colour of the current style, editable live. Tune a style here, then click "Export" to copy the C++ code that sets it (lesson 4.05).

## The Metrics/Debugger window

```cpp-norun
ImGui::ShowMetricsWindow();
```

It shows ImGui's own state: every window with its position, size and draw list (how many vertices, how many draw commands), the active and hovered widget IDs, the ID stack, the font atlas, tables' internal state, and more. Hover a draw command and it highlights what it draws. Use it when:

- the interface is slow (which window has thousands of vertices?);
- something is drawn but you cannot see why (where is its clip rectangle?);
- a window behaves oddly (what are its flags and size constraints?).

## The ID Stack tool

```cpp-norun
ImGui::ShowIDStackToolWindow();
```

Hover any widget: it shows the ID stack for it, level by level - the window's seed, every `PushID`, the label - and the final ID. The fastest way to understand why two widgets clash (lesson 1.05).

## The Item Picker

In the Metrics window, **Tools, Item Picker**: click any widget in your program, and ImGui stops in the debugger **inside the code that drew it**. When you have a complex tool and cannot find which of fifty functions draws a misbehaving checkbox, this finds it in one click.

## Debug log

The Metrics window has a **Debug Log** section that records what ImGui does in categories you choose: focus changes, popups, navigation, I/O events, docking. Turn on "I/O" and you see every mouse and keyboard event the back end feeds in, which answers "is ImGui even receiving my input?".

## Assertions are your friends

ImGui uses `IM_ASSERT` heavily: unmatched `Begin`/`End`, `PushID`/`PopID`, calls outside a frame, bad parameters. In a Debug build the debugger stops on the exact line, with a comment in the source explaining the rule you broke. Read the comment above the assert; it nearly always says what to do. You can route assertions to your own handler by defining `IM_ASSERT` in `imconfig.h`.

## Common mistakes

> [!warning] Guessing instead of looking
> When a widget misbehaves, the ID Stack tool, the Metrics window and the Item Picker usually find the cause in seconds.

> [!warning] Disabling assertions to make a crash go away
> The assert is reporting a real mistake that will cause worse problems later. Fix the pairing or the call order instead.

## Check yourself
```quiz
? Which list names debugging tools built into ImGui?
- ShowDemoWindow, the Visual Studio profiler, PIX and RenderDoc
+ ShowDemoWindow, the style editor, the Metrics/Debugger window (with its debug log and Item Picker), and the ID Stack tool
- The Metrics window, the ID Stack tool, the Win32 back end log and imgui.ini viewer
> All four ship with ImGui itself and open from the demo window's Tools menu. Profilers and graphics debuggers are separate programs.

? What should you do when an IM_ASSERT fires?
- Define IM_ASSERT as nothing in imconfig.h so the program keeps running
- Restart the program; asserts usually come from a race between frames
+ Read the comment above it in the source, which explains the rule, and fix the code that broke it
> The assert reports a real mistake (an unmatched Begin/End or PushID/PopID, a call outside a frame). Silencing it only moves the crash elsewhere.

? Why keep imgui_demo.cpp in the project during development?
- ImGui will not compile or link without its definitions
+ It shows every feature, and costs nothing unless ShowDemoWindow is called
- It sets up the default style, which every other window needs
> Find a feature in the demo window, then search imgui_demo.cpp for its label to see the code. Leave the call out of shipping builds.

? What is the quickest way to find example code for a widget you saw in ShowDemoWindow?
+ Search imgui_demo.cpp for the label shown in the demo
- Read imgui.cpp from the top
- Open the Metrics window and look for the widget's code there
> The demo is the documentation, with its source beside it.

? Which tool tells you why two widgets share an ID?
- The style editor
+ The ID Stack tool
- The font atlas viewer in the Metrics window
> It shows each level of the ID stack for the hovered widget: the window's seed, every PushID and the label.

? You cannot find which function draws a misbehaving widget. What helps?
- The Debug Log with the I/O category turned on, to trace clicks
- The style editor's Export button, to dump each widget's source
+ The Item Picker, which breaks into the code that drew the widget you click
> It is in the Metrics window's Tools and breaks into the debugger at the drawing code. The I/O debug log shows input events, not where a widget is drawn.
```
ideas:
- Open the demo window, find "Widgets, Sliders", and copy one slider from `imgui_demo.cpp` into your own window.
- Open the Metrics window and find your "Stones" window's vertex count; add a hundred stones and watch it grow.
- Use the Item Picker on one of your buttons.
